en: Title: The Twelve Names of Mahāśrī Source: Hidas & Szántó, 84000 Tibetan: D 741 [=1006]

[3] <1v> Homage to Tārā! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sukhāvatī. Then the Blessed One, having seen Mahāśrī, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Mañjuśrī and Āryāvalokiteśvara as follows: "Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, whoever—whether a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, or anyone else—shall know the twelve names of the goddess Mahāśrī, or shall uphold, recite, write, or cause them to be written, for that person there will be no fear of poverty. Having abandoned poverty, they will become wealthy. Then the Blessed One spoke the twelve names of the goddess Mahāśrī, as follows: Oṃ Lakṣmī, Śrī, Padmamālinī, Dhanādhipati, Gaurī, Mahāyaśā, Padmanetrī, Kartrī, Mahādyuti, Annadāyinī, Ratnaprabhā, and Mahāśrī. Herein are the mantra-words: *jini 2 glini 2 kāyaviśodhani vāgviśodhani manaḥsaṃśodhani | sisi sisi | nimi 2 alakṣmīṃ me nāśaya svāhā*. [The rest is lost. *Mahāśrī-nāma-dhāraṇī*

[40] [Siddham] Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sukhāvatī. Then the Blessed One, having beheld Mahāśrī, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Mañjuśrī and Āryāvalokiteśvara: "Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, whoever—whether a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, or anyone else—shall know the twelve names of the goddess Mahāśrī, or shall uphold, recite, write, or cause them to be written, for him there shall be no fear of poverty. Having abandoned poverty, he shall become wealthy. Then the Blessed One spoke the twelve names of the goddess Mahāśrī: namely, Oṃ Lakṣmī, Śrī, Padmamālinī, Dhanādhipati, Gaurī, Mahāyaśā, Padmanetrī, Karttrī, Mahādyuti, Annadāyinī, Ratnaprabhā, and Mahāśrī. Herein are the mantra-words: *jini jini, gliṇi gliṇi, kāyaviśodhani, vāgviśodhani, manaḥsaṃśodhani, sisi sisi, nimi nimi, alakṣmīṃ me nāśaya svāhā*. This should be recited three times. Whoever shall utter it, all his adversaries shall perish; he shall become fortunate. It should be recited when seeing a king; the king will come under his influence and, regarding him as a son, will do whatever he says. By constant recitation, Mahābrahmā comes; having arrived, he grants whatever boon one desires. The Blessed One said this, and Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, and the entire assembly—including gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken. Thus ends the Noble Dhāraṇī of the Names of Mahāśrī.
